description: F257 — the self-use queue Remedy runs against its own repository. Operator-curated DATA, not discovery: Remedy never invents an item and never appends one. # Job: Document the Markdown job-file format

## Task 1
Write one new page under `docs/` describing the Markdown job-file format that
`packages/orchestration/pingpong_job.py:parse_job_file` accepts, so a reader
looking for the format finds it where the documentation index sends them.

The page states, at minimum: the `# Job: <title>` H1 that names the job; the
`## Task N` headings that split the file into tasks; and the `Acceptance:` line
that separates a task's body from its acceptance criteria. Describe what the
parser really does rather than what a reader might assume — task ids are
assigned by parse order (T001, T002, ...) and not by the heading number, which
is kept separately. Cite the parser by path so the page can be checked against
the code it describes.

Register the new page in the `docs/README.md` index with its category, a
one-line description and a status marker, the way AGENTS.md's Documentation
Updates rules require of every new ist-doc.

Acceptance:
- A new page under `docs/` describes the job-file format, naming the `# Job:` H1, the `## Task N` headings and the `Acceptance:` line.
- That page is registered in the `docs/README.md` index with a category, a one-line description and a status marker.

items.title: Give apps/ui's ESLint config a TypeScript parser (R-0622)
items.why: Registered as finding R-0622 (Medium, OPEN) in .agent/live_review.md. Re-measured fresh on the amend0829-selfuse-v2 branch: `apps/ui/eslint.config.js` selects `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` and enables `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`'s recommended rules, but sets no `languageOptions.parser` and `apps/ui/package.json` ships no `typescript-eslint` in dependencies or devDependencies. Running `npm run --silent lint` in `apps/ui` now exits 1 with 109 problems (107 errors, 2 warnings), every one a `Parsing error` on the first TypeScript-only syntax the default JS parser hits (the finding measured 47 errors at 22dd8d31; the count has grown as more `.ts`/`.tsx` files shipped since). The rule set that never evaluates as a result includes `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`, which is exactly the rule that would catch a stale-closure bug in a reconnecting hook. Small, bounded — a devDependency and a config block — genuinely useful, and it touches no path the scope fences deny. `npm run lint` is not part of any gate this repository runs (reviewer convention: never gate on `npm run lint`), so this is pure paydown with no interaction with the review machinery.

items.title: Give FailureClass a RESOURCE_LIMIT member (R-0568)
items.why: Registered as finding R-0568 (Medium, OPEN) in .agent/live_review.md. Re-measured fresh on the amend0829-selfuse-v2 branch: `packages/orchestration/exec_guard.py:504,506,508` sets `classification = "resource_limit"` (with `tripped_limit` naming `wall_timeout`, `cpu_seconds` or `output_bytes`) when a guarded execution is killed by its own limit, but `packages/orchestration/failure_postmortem.py`'s `FailureClass` enum has no `RESOURCE_LIMIT` member — `python3 -c "from packages.orchestration.failure_postmortem import FailureClass; print(list(FailureClass))"` lists 15 members and none is resource-limit shaped. `failure_postmortem.classify()` (line 304) has no branch that reads `tripped_limit` or a `resource_limit` classification at all, so a run killed by its own wall-clock, CPU or output-byte limit is postmortemed as `UNKNOWN` rather than as the resource-limit trip it measurably was. Both the F010 postmortem taxonomy's Design section and the F085 feature file document this as in-scope but never wired up. Small, bounded (one enum member plus one classify() branch plus a fixture), genuinely useful, and it touches no path the scope fences deny.

# Job: Give FailureClass a RESOURCE_LIMIT member

## Task 1
In `packages/orchestration/failure_postmortem.py`, add a `RESOURCE_LIMIT` member to the `FailureClass` enum (value `"resource_limit"`, matching the string `exec_guard.py` already emits). Add a branch to `classify()` (or to whatever `FailureSignals` producer feeds it) that reads an `ExecGuardResult` whose `classification == "resource_limit"` and returns `FailureClass.RESOURCE_LIMIT`, carrying the `tripped_limit` value (`wall_timeout` / `cpu_seconds` / `output_bytes`) into the classification's detail text so the postmortem names which limit tripped.

## Task 2
Add a test fixture that runs a guarded execution killed by each of the three limits (`wall_timeout`, `cpu_seconds`, `output_bytes`) and asserts the resulting postmortem is classified `FailureClass.RESOURCE_LIMIT` with the correct limit named, alongside the existing fixture proving the unrelated classes are unaffected.

Acceptance:
- `FailureClass` has a `RESOURCE_LIMIT` member.
- A guarded execution killed by `wall_timeout`, `cpu_seconds`, or `output_bytes` is postmortemed as `RESOURCE_LIMIT`, not `UNKNOWN`, with the tripped limit named.
- Existing failure-classification tests stay green.
